title: From $0 to $100K: Every Step, In Order
description:
Getting from $0 to $100,000 has an order, and most people do it backwards. This is every step, in the right order: emergency fund, debt, retirement match, investing, and the habits that carry you through the slow middle.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:21 How we got the numbers
2:07 Angle 1: The numbers
4:38 Step 1. Know your numbers
5:47 Step 2. A starter emergency fund
6:49 Step 3. Get the full employer match
7:56 Step 4. Kill high interest debt
9:08 Step 5. A full emergency fund
10:21 Step 6. Automate and raise your rate
11:43 Step 7. Open an IRA
13:01 Step 8. Invest simply and cheaply
14:11 Step 9. Control the big three
15:17 Step 10. Grow your income
16:18 Step 11. Beat lifestyle creep
17:26 Step 12. Stay the course
18:37 Finding your first $300 a month
20:22 Angle 2: The psychology
22:26 Angle 3: The playbook
24:38 What every milestone feels like
27:12 Five mistakes on the way
28:03 Questions people ask
30:09 Recap: 12 steps in order
31:31 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (63% would cover a $400 expense with cash or its equivalent)
- Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit (credit card interest rates above 20%)
- IRS, 401(k) and IRA contribution limits and catch-up contributions (check current-year limits)
- S&P Dow Jones Indices, SPIVA U.S. Scorecard (most active funds trail their benchmark over long periods)
- Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Expenditure Survey (housing, transportation and food are the largest spending categories)
- Kahneman and Tversky, Prospect Theory, Econometrica (1979) (losses loom larger than gains)
- Compound growth: stated illustrative math at 7% average yearly return, compounded monthly

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video05.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
